title: mercury-brokers-batched-rerank-throughput-diary-2028-03
summary: Field-style run diary for a Solutions Eng POC with Mercury Brokers: evaluate batched reranking workload (short queries, 3-8 tokens rerank score outputs) for cost/throughput/latency tradeoffs. Primary objective: identify batching parameters and model variant that meet p95 <= 120ms while maximizing sustained queries/sec and minimizing GPU cost per 1M queries.
background: Mercury Brokers is building a latencies-sensitive market-feed personalization pipeline: upstream candidates (10–50) per request, we run a lightweight reranker to score top 5. They require p95 <= 120ms at steady-state QPS of 800 for peak trading windows, with an operational budget constraint of <$2000 GPU-hours per month. This diary captures iterative lab runs we performed on their workload trace (synthetic replay from their prod-ish capture dated 2028-02-11).
test_plan:
- Workload: replay of 1200s trace with adjustable QPS envelopes (steady 200/400/800 with 30s microbursts to 2000 QPS).
- Models: rerank-small-v2 (fp16), rerank-small-v2-q4 (4-bit quant), rerank-medium (fp16) for baseline.
- Runtime: Redwood Dedicated nodes (A100-40GB); experiments with 1–4 nodes.
- Batching knobs: max_batch_size {8,16,32,64}, max_wait_ms {3,6,12,24}.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 generation latency (end-to-end), tail queue wait, GPU util, tokens/sec, cost per 1M requests (estimated from GPU-hour usage).
- Run cadence: sequential parameter sweeps, warmup 5min, measurement 10min per configuration.
env_config:
- Node: A100-40GB, 8 vCPU, 64GB RAM per node; kubernetes pool w/elastic autoscaler turned off for runs.
- Runtime: Redwood serving runtime v2.9.1 with batching pipeline and prefix cache disabled unless noted.
- Quantization: q4run used for rerank-small-v2-q4 via Redwood Optimize recommendations.
- Network: colocated in us-west-2; latency noise baseline ~1.5ms.
- Replay harness: custom runner (github link above) that preserves inter-arrival times and candidate counts from Mercury trace.
run_log:
2028-03-15 09:10 UTC: initial smoke -> rerank-small-v2, 1 node, batch_size 32, wait 12ms -> p95 210ms (too high), queue wait dominated.
2028-03-15 09:35 UTC: reduced batch_size 16, wait 6ms -> p95 145ms; GPU util ~62%.
2028-03-15 10:05 UTC: tried q4 quant (rerank-small-v2-q4), batch_size 32, wait 12ms -> p95 130ms, p99 290ms (p99 bad, occasional heavy microburst misses).
2028-03-15 11:00 UTC: added node (2 nodes total), batch_size 32, wait 12ms with q4 -> steady p95 95ms, p99 160ms, throughput sustained 1.9k qps across nodes (peak burst absorb ~2k for 40s). GPU util per node ~74%.
2028-03-16 14:20 UTC: stress sweep with 3 nodes and batch_size 64, wait 24ms -> p95 105ms but cold microbursts produced p99 >400ms due to queueing and GC; not acceptable.
2028-03-18 08:00 UTC: final recommended config tested: rerank-small-v2-q4, 2 nodes, batch_size 32, wait 8ms -> p95 110ms, p99 170ms, cost estimate 1.6 GPU-hours per 1M queries (projected), meets p95 target and budget headroom.
raw_results:
Sample matrix (summary):
- rerank-small-v2 (fp16) 1 node: batch32/wait12 -> p50 18ms, p95 210ms, p99 360ms, qps sustained 850 (throttling at burst), GPU util 68%, est cost 2.4 GPU-hrs / 1M q.
- rerank-small-v2 (fp16) 2 nodes: batch32/wait12 -> p50 12ms, p95 135ms, p99 240ms, qps 1700, GPU util 72%, est cost 2.0 GPU-hrs / 1M q.
- rerank-small-v2-q4 1 node: batch32/wait12 -> p50 15ms, p95 130ms, p99 290ms, qps 1100, GPU util 55%, est cost 1.5 GPU-hrs / 1M q.
- rerank-small-v2-q4 2 nodes: batch32/wait8 -> p50 10ms, p95 110ms, p99 170ms, qps 1900, GPU util 74%, est cost 1.6 GPU-hrs / 1M q.
- rerank-medium fp16 2 nodes: batch16/wait6 -> p95 220ms (too slow), qps 700, est cost 3.6 GPU-hrs / 1M q.
Observations: quantized variant reduces per-sample compute but increases variance under microbursts due to slightly longer kernel tail behavior in our runtime version.
analysis:
Key takeaways:
- Best cost/latency tradeoff: rerank-small-v2-q4 on 2 nodes with batch_size 32 and wait 8ms. This meets p95 <= 120ms at sustained 800–900 QPS and survives microbursts to ~2k QPS for short periods.
- Single-node configs can support ~1k sustained QPS but fail the p95 requirement during microbursts; autoscaling or adding concurrency headroom is necessary.
- Larger max_batch_size (>=64) increases throughput but hurts tail latency; microburst periods amplify this effect due to queueing.
- Quantization saved ~25–35% GPU-hour cost per 1M queries in steady-state, but introduced heavier p99 tails in certain kernel paths — mitigated by smaller max_wait_ms and extra node headroom.
- GPU utilization sweet spot observed at ~70–80% per node; below that we waste cost, above it tail latency rises.

Risks / unknowns:
- Production trace may have different candidate distributions; we used Mercury's captured trace but recommend a second replay from a separate day with heavy candidate counts.
- Runtime v2.9.1 shows some p99 artifacts in quantized kernels; Redwood runtime team has a queued PR to adjust kernel launch batching (linked above).
recommendations:
1) Short-term (2–4 weeks): onboard Mercury to Dedicated plan with a 2-node A100 pool, initial config: rerank-small-v2-q4, max_batch_size 32, max_wait_ms 8, enable autoscale policy to add one node if sustained QPS >1600 for 3m.
2) Observability: instrument per-route queue wait histograms, token-level cost breakdown, and warm-start prefix cache for rerank candidates.
3) Cost ops: model quantization should be used by default, but gate q4 on a canary A/B split to monitor p99 before full rollout. Keep fp16 fallback route for seconds of peak overload.
4) Follow up tests: rerun with replay day B and candidate cardinality increased by +25% to stress candidate-side cost; test with runtime v2.10 once kernel PR merges.

conclusion: We can meet Mercury Brokers' p95 latency target and cost goals using a quantized reranker on a 2-node Dedicated pool with modest batching limits. Actionable next step is a short canary rollout with observability gates and a follow-up replay to validate candidate distribution variability.
